title: Bulk re-key: one admin-authorised rotate across a named set of externalRefs
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for **one** admin-authorised action that re-keys a named set of Organisations by `externalRef`, instead of N separate `register-connector` calls during an incident. The loop itself is **1–2 days**.

**It must not ship before** [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) **(revoke-on-rotate).** Built on today's additive rotate, a bulk re-key would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and *look* like recovery.

## Detail

Today's single-org path is `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` with `rotate: true` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476-729`:

* platform-admin only; guardrail 1 refuses a connector-authorised rotate with 403 (`:499-509`)
* resolves the org by `metadata->>'externalRef'` under platform scope (`:590-593`)
* mints a fresh `sk_` key via the security service (`:674-686` → `services/security/src/index.ts:800`)
* plaintext key returned exactly once (`:719-720`)

`runWithPlatformScope` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:102`) already handles the cross-tenant access, so multi-tenancy is **not** the hard part here.

**Scope**

* Extract `platform.ts:476-729` into a reusable per-org function; add a bulk route taking a list of `externalRef`s.
* Return a **per-ref result array** — partial success must be explicit. An incident operator has to know which refs failed and why.
* OpenAPI entry + `generate-openapi` regen + api-gateway rebuild (the gateway bakes the spec) + KS-380 preflight.

**Explicitly out of scope:** delivery of the key material for N keys. One response body carrying N live secrets is not the answer; that needs its own design and a security review (see the KS-480 sizing table).

**Cheaper alternative on the record** (raised because @peter asked not to have the manual path assumed away): a scripted loop over the existing admin endpoint gives one *operator action* today at near-zero build cost. It does not give one *authorisation*, which is the part actually being asked for.

**Done when:** an admin can re-key a named set of refs in one authorised call, each prior key is revoked per the [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) semantics, per-ref outcomes are explicit, and the [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) rehearsal passes all four steps.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled on 2026-11-10 that the bulk re-key takes the grant-driven shape: a platform admin mints a time-boxed grant and Platform S re-keys itself. Nothing is built from this comment.

**What was ruled.** Card `secuura-ks576-bulk-rekey-shape-1109`, option a: "Grant-driven: admin mints a time-boxed grant, S re-keys itself (Stuart's proposal)". The proposal is comment 033cf92e on this ticket (2026-09-02). PS-740 is the Platform S half (comment eda75bbe).

**The card's own limit.** "No build before the design returns to you." The card also asks for the design to be sized for KS-576 and KS-582; that sizing is not started by this comment.

**What this does not do.** It does not start a build, change this ticket's state or priority, or lift the ticket's own condition that it must not ship before KS-577 (revoke-on-rotate). KS-577 stays In Review.

Re-filed as its own issue now the cap has cleared: **[PS-740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-740/sk-key-recovery-a-keyinvalid-state-a-supported-inlet-for-a-rotated)** — the S-side half of the grant-driven re-key (KeyInvalid state, rotated-key inlet, grant drain, expiry visibility). Linked Related from here.

## Proposal from the S side: make the re-key **grant-driven**, with S as the executor

Context: investigating key expiry/recovery after S's local provisioning key lapsed on 2026-08-31 (PS-319). Verified in code on both sides, S today has **no recovery path at all** — re-registration returns no key (§4), `rotate: true` is 403'd for a provisioning-key caller by Guardrail 1 (`platform.ts:503`), and even an admin-run rotation dead-ends because S has no inlet to receive the key (`EncryptedApiKey` is written only by the registrar's first mint). The full S-side write-up is on PS-319 (pending re-file as its own ticket — the workspace issue cap is hit).

**The shape.** Keep Guardrail 1's human-in-the-loop, but change *who executes*:

1. A platform admin mints a **re-key grant** — one-time, time-boxed (hours), naming an explicit list of `externalRef`s (or all-for-tenant), recorded as its own audited object.
2. `register-connector` accepts `rotate: true` from a **provisioning-scoped** caller **only when accompanied by a live grant** covering that `externalRef`; the grant is consumed per ref. Revoke-on-rotate (KS-577) folded in.
3. S's registration sweep, given the grant via its secret store, drains every dead-key row itself and stores the returned keys exactly as first registration does.

**Why this over the admin-executed bulk endpoint as currently scoped:** with the admin executing, N plaintext keys come back to a human who then has to get them into S — a path S does not even have today, and one that puts operational secrets through hands and clipboards. With S executing under a grant, plaintext never leaves the two systems, the *same* mechanism recovers a **greenfield S against a populated K** (the `AlreadyRegistered`-no-key terminal case from S's DR facts), and the grant *is* the approval artifact KS-582 is asking for.

**It answers KS-582's open questions directly:** approver = whoever mints the grant (two-approver batch = a grant needing two mints/co-signs once KS-579 gives per-person admins; one for a single-ref grant); the flow is request → approve (grant minted) → execute (S drains), with the grant as the record between steps; the ref list is fixed at mint, so it cannot be edited after approval; break-glass is the existing S-side `UseConnectorKeyAuth=false` fallback, already alarmed three ways, so no new break-glass path is needed here.

**Input for Stuart's KS-577 cutover question** (his decision, not mine): when S is the executor, the cutover window collapses — S holds the new key the instant the response lands and the old one is revoked in the same operation; anything in flight in that sub-second gap 401s once and is retried by the refresher, which already handles exactly that. No grace window needed.

**Companion ask, small and independent:** a `whoami`-style read returning the *calling* key's id/scopes/`expiresAt`. Nothing today lets a key learn when it expires, so S cannot warn ahead — the 08-31 lapse was invisible until it bit.
